retag.stanceId: research citation (live /api/research tag) on https://www.xavierbecerra2026.com/priorities/ , 'Energy and Utilities' section
retag.quote: I believe that by treating clean energy and grid resilience as public investments—and ensuring renters, low-income households, and workers share in the benefits—California can fight climate change, strengthen reliability, and make energy more affordable for everyone.
retag.why: The quote is about clean energy, the grid and climate. 'Workers' is incidental. A clear pro-renewables statement scores +3, which matches the stored stances.json energy +3 ('California’s clean-energy transition is necessary and urgent').
retag.note: stances.json is unaffected: Becerra energy +3 and wages +3 (LAist living-wage quote) are already correctly tagged. The mis-tag lives only in the research/model citation layer.

xavier-becerra.opponentConsistency: Steve Hilton is scored on the same kind of evidence (campaign-page statements, e.g. energy −5 from his $3-gas plan page). No other ca-gov candidate scored differently on comparable evidence. Related research-layer suspect: Hilton's CBS quote ('$3 gas, your first $150,000 tax-free, capping vehicle registration…') is tagged housing, but it is mostly taxes/energy (see suspects).

suspects.quote: This has to involve massive cuts in the federal budget in every single program and department.
suspects.why: A general spending/tax-cut statement with no infrastructure content. Better as taxes (or drop). Clear mismatch.

suspects.quote: My focus will be on allocating funding for housing, healthcare, and programs such as SNAP.
suspects.why: No safety content in the quote. It is valid as diversion only if the NYC Votes question was about public safety (page is JS-rendered, context not verifiable here).

suspects.quote: …no reason we shouldn't be able to meet and exceed the needs of every Texan who wants a home, healthcare, and good public schools.
suspects.why: About services, not taxes. Taxes direction is inferred.
School discipline, not policing/prosecution (the safety axis).

suspects.quote: I fully support Free City and the grant program, and strongly oppose any cuts or reductions to the program.
suspects.why: Program support, not a tax position.

suspects.quote: Free City is crucial and must not be a political bargaining chip.
I believe in the free market, where people freely trade with each other without government regulations and controls.
suspects.why: Generic free-market statement; does not mention wages. Direction is plausible but inferred.

suspects.quote: All need to be held responsible! I believe the data centers will be more of the same.
suspects.why: Vague; the energy direction depends on surrounding context.

suspects.quote: We know that the state needs improved grid reliability…
suspects.why: Not a tag mismatch: the same quote is +3 in stances.json and +2 in accountability.json. Pick one.

suspects.quote: $3 gas, your first $150,000 tax-free, capping vehicle registration…

suspects.why: See the xavier-becerra entry: should be energy.

suspectsMethod: Keyword scan of all scored stances.json quotes: flagged a quote when it has no keyword for its tagged issue, or another issue's keywords dominate by 2 or more. 70 + 15 hits, reviewed by hand. Most were fine (e.g. ACA tax credits → healthcare, SB 54 → immigration). Only the entries above were kept. jon-rosenthal energy ('Texas Green New Deal') was checked and is correct. Nothing was changed.
